SetVersion version 2.xx by Mikero.<br> <br>
see readme general<br>
see fixes

 
----
 
<br>
SerVersion changes the RequiredVersion= of any config.cpp/bin within an 
addon.pbo<br> <br> <br>
It is specifically targetted at (but not limited to) making Arma ONE addons 
compatible with Arma TWO.<br> <br> <br>
For the most part this will work, because. for the most part, the engine 
'understands' the alternate p3d compressions (lzss) inside arma1. And / Or, the 
p3d models and classes are largely in the same /ca/folder/ network.<br> <br>
As an aside, but, for the removal of some half dozen objects in the arma2 addons, 
sara, and most missions would have been compatible with a2. There is no readily 
available upgrade path, rendering all previous efforts and mission creation, 
redundant. So much for a retaining a loyal customer base. <br> <br>
Secondly, why on earth each revision of the engine from cwc through to arma2 has 
revision values LESS than previous engines defies all explanation.<br> <br>
------<br>
Useage<br> <br>
SetVersion [-options] 1.03(eg) SomePbo[.pbo] [AnotherPbo[.pbo]]<br> <br>
options<br> <br>
-x Exclude config.cpp(s) from revision. only revise bin<br>
-p dont pause

 
<br>
note that SetVersion is recursive. It will change ALL config.cpp/bins's 
encountered in the pbo<br> <br> <br>
Return Values<br>
--------------<br> <br>
for Dos usage it is useful to 'know' (via ERRORLEVEL) what operation was 
performed<br> <br>
0 VERSION_CHANGED: a change took place<br>
1 VERSION_SAME: the RequiredVersion(s) are identical to what was wanted no 
change to pbo<br>
2 VERSION_NONE: no config(s) (or no RequiredVersion= in those configs) found. no 
change to pbo<br>
3 VERSION_ERROR: file could not be processed in some way<br> <br> <br> <br> <br>
***************<br>
CAVEAT EMPTOR and ROE (rules of engagement)<br>
***************<br> <br>
Config.cpp<br> <br>
Config.cpp is normally a text file. It can, alternatively be encountered in a 
binarised form, and to all intents is a config.bin<br> <br> <br>
When config.cpp IS a text file, SetVersion attempts to convert it 'on the fly' 
to a binarised form<br> <br>
This conversion will fail if paths are incorrect for #include statements (eg). 
Generally, any binarisation of a config requires that you set up a P: drive<br> <br>
You also may not wish to do this for several reasons. You can use the -x option 
to prevent setversion changing config.cpp's<br> <br> <br>
HOWEVER<br>
if allowed, and IF encountered, and IF successful, the original 'file' is 
renamed to config.cpp.txt, and a new text file replaces it. THIS, NEW text file<br>
will be stripped of all comments and #includes (because they are unecessary at 
this point)<br> <br> <br> <br>
Note finally, that this is a kludge. Redundant hpp files and included cpp text 
files will remain in the pbo, where, normally, these too would be removed during 
the rapification process.<br> <br>
